paper_title: ThermoDSE: A Thermal-Aware and Comprehensive Design Space Exploration for Chiplet-Based DNN Accelerators

scenario.figure_or_table: Table IV, row 'Ours' (thermal map in Fig. 10(b), PDF page 12)
scenario.description: ThermoDSE-optimized 2.5D chiplet DNN accelerator: 5x4 NPU cores split into 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm inter-chiplet spacing, 240 GB/s NoC/NoP bandwidth, 1024 KB uniform buffer and 208x112 systolic array per core. Reported results: peak temperature 74.8 C, energy 59.8 mJ, delay 2.01 ms, yield 0.911, EDYP 132.2. Thermal evaluation used HotSpot 6.0 steady-state with a 300 mm2 interposer area limit and a 75 C peak-temperature limit. The packet contains no per-block coordinates, dimensions, or power values.
scenario.architecture: Chiplet-based DNN accelerator (Arch-S, fine-grained task orchestration across chiplets): 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array, 240 GB/s NoC bandwidth; 14 nm scaled, 1.8 GHz
scenario.workload: AR/VR multi-DNN mix: ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net, BERT-Small (batch sizes per Table III)
scenario.operating_point: 1.8 GHz, 14 nm, HotSpot 6.0 steady-state, ambient 45 C, convection resistance 0.4 K/W, 300 mm2 interposer limit, 75 C peak limit; reported peak temperature 74.8 C

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal simulation (PDF p.4, p.7) using component-wise average power, floorplan and material properties. Performance, energy and yield come from a custom simulator with fine-grained µtask orchestration. Ambient 45 C, convection resistance 0.4 K/W, TIM, heat spreader and heat sink properties adopted from TESA (PDF p.7, p.9).
original_setup.optimizer: TED (transductive experimental design) initialization plus SCBO (scalable constrained Bayesian optimization, BoTorch) minimizing EDYP = E x D / Y under a 75 C peak-temperature limit and a 300 mm2 interposer-area limit (PDF p.7-9). Compared with SA (TESA) and PPO-based RL (Chiplet-Gym) (PDF p.12, Table V).
original_setup.controller: No runtime thermal controller. DVFS is discussed as unsuitable (PDF p.3). Thermal management is design-time only: greedy thermal-aware task mapping puts high-power µtasks on corner cores and low-power ones on center cores (PDF p.5), plus inter-chiplet spacing as a cooling knob.
original_setup.benchmark: AR/VR multi-DNN mix of ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, MobileNetv2, Yolov2, U-Net and BERT-Small (Table III, PDF p.9), run sequentially at 1.8 GHz in 14 nm. Selected scenario: the 'Ours' row of Table IV (PDF p.10): 5x4 NPU cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS, 1024 KB uniform buffer, 208x112 systolic array, 240 GB/s NoC. Reported energy 59.8 mJ, delay 2.01 ms, yield 0.911, EDYP 132.2. Thermal map in Fig. 10(b) (PDF p.12).

thermal_observable.location: Peak temperature of the chiplet-based accelerator, from HotSpot 6.0 on the interposer-level floorplan of the ThermoDSE-optimized design
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (peak) steady-state temperature over the floorplan, using component-wise average power over the AR/VR workload mix

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 2.5D multi-chiplet system on an interposer with NoP/D2D links, die-to-die spacing (ICS 2.3 mm) and a TIM/heat spreader/heat sink stack. A simple 2D single-die runner cannot reproduce the inter-chiplet lateral coupling, interposer heat spreading or NoP power distribution.

The power input is an average derived from analytical energy/latency models over a sequential multi-DNN workload. It is not a transient power trace, and the paper models no transient thermal behavior, only steady state.

The paper does not publish per-block floorplan coordinates, block dimensions or per-block power for the selected design. Only aggregate parameters are given: core/chiplet counts, ICS, buffer size, systolic array size, and total energy and delay. A block-level replication is therefore impossible.

The optimizer is TED+SCBO Bayesian optimization co-optimizing architecture and task mapping, with no runtime controller. A Studio runner has no equivalent optimizer, so only the thermal solve could be exercised.
The cooling model (convection resistance 0.4 K/W, 45 C ambient, TESA material properties) and the HotSpot 6.0 package stack may differ from the Studio's bundled material and package assumptions.
Reliability is not modeled beyond the 75 C peak limit. Yield is modeled analytically from die area and is unrelated to thermal reliability.

studio_assumptions: No paper-derived floorplan exists, so any runner placement would be a separately generated illustrative 2D layout with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper facts.
Studio uses its own bundled package and material stack, which is not guaranteed to match the paper's HotSpot 6.0 interposer/TIM/spreader/heat-sink configuration (TESA properties).
Studio runs a 2D thermal solve, not the paper's 2.5D interposer model.
Any one-row power trace would be illustrative only, and Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 74.8 C.
missing_inputs: No linked assets, repositories, supplementary data or code. The artifact search found no links and the packet asset list is empty.
Per-block x_m, y_m, width_m and height_m for the selected design (5x4 cores in 1x2 chiplets, 2.3 mm ICS). Fig. 10 shows only an area breakdown and thermal map with no coordinates.
Per-block power_rows (name and watts) for the selected design. Only total energy (59.8 mJ) and delay (2.01 ms) are published, with no published rule for splitting power across blocks.
Material properties and package parameters (TIM, heat spreader, heat sink dimensions and conductivities). These are cited to TESA [12] but not given in the packet.
Compute die area, I/O die area and interposer layout details for the 2-chiplet design.
Time-resolved power trace or per-network power breakdown.

evidence.locator: Table IV, row 'Ours', column Temp.(°C)
evidence.provenance: Paper-reported peak temperature of the ThermoDSE-optimized design from HotSpot 6.0 steady state. It is the maximum over the floorplan, using component-wise average power over the AR/VR mix. Location is the interposer-level floorplan; no hotspot coordinates are given.
evidence.uncertainty: Tabulated value; no error bar. Hotspot location not stated in the table, and Fig. 10(b) is only a qualitative thermal map.
